title: Meeting people: introductions and be
lessonNotes: Introduce yourself and keep a conversation moving with a follow-up question.
Use am / is / are for identity, location, feelings and jobs.
Read phone numbers clearly, one digit at a time; double is also useful for repeated digits.

sections.label: Grammar: am / is / are
sections.intro: Use the verb be to say who someone is, where they are, or how they feel. The form changes with the subject.

rules.label: Positive
rules.body: I am (I'm); you / we / they are; he / she / it is.

rules.label: Negative
rules.body: Put not after be: am not, is not (isn't), are not (aren't).

rules.label: Questions
rules.body: Put am / is / are before the subject. Answer with a short form when possible.
examples: Are you from Istanbul? — Yes, I am.
Is she married? — No, she isn't.

sections.label: Grammar exercises
sections.intro: Choose an answer. You can try again if you need to.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: I ___ from Izmir.

questions.explanation: Put are before you in a be question.
Use is with she: She is not married.

sections.label: Vocabulary flashcards
sections.intro: Select a card to turn it over. Read the English meaning, Turkish translation and example.

items.explanation: A friendly phrase when you meet someone for the first time.
items.example: Hi, I'm Elif. Nice to meet you.

items.explanation: Use it to ask about a person's home country or city.
items.example: Where are you from? — I'm from Bursa.

items.explanation: A question about hobbies and interests.
items.example: What do you like doing? — I like reading.

items.explanation: A phone number someone can use to contact you.
The country group a person belongs to, for example Turkish or American.

items.example: He is single. They are married.

sections.label: Vocabulary exercises
sections.intro: Use the meaning and examples from the flashcards.

questions.explanation: What do you like doing? asks about interests.

questions.prompt: Choose the best reply: Nice to meet you.
questions.explanation: Nice to meet you too is the natural polite reply.
It is a number people can use to call or message you.

sections.label: Listening: meeting other students
sections.sourceLabel: British Council LearnEnglish — A1: Meeting other students
sections.body: Open the listening, do the preparation task, then listen once for the main idea and once for names, places and study subjects. Complete the British Council tasks there before answering the quick checks below.

questions.prompt: In the listening, what phrase do the students use when they first meet?
questions.explanation: Listen for the introduction between the new students.

questions.prompt: Which kind of information do the students share?
questions.explanation: The conversation includes questions about where people are from.

sections.label: Reading: a first conversation
sections.body: Hi, I'm Deniz. Nice to meet you. I'm from Ankara, but I'm in Berlin today for a design course. I'm a designer and I like reading, coffee and city walks. My friend Ece is here too. She is from Izmir and she is very interested in art. We are not in the same class, but we are both happy to meet new people. What do you like doing?
sections.prompt: Read once for the general idea, then read again and answer the questions.

questions.prompt: Are Deniz and Ece in the same class?
questions.explanation: They are not in the same class.

quiz.prompt: Choose the natural answer: Where are you from?
quiz.explanation: Use from + place to give your origin.

quiz.prompt: Choose the correct sentence for a location now.
quiz.explanation: I am in + place describes where you are.

quiz.prompt: Which is a good follow-up after ‘I like reading’?
quiz.explanation: Ask about the detail the person just mentioned.
What do you like doing? is the complete question.
